summary: This is a Mol Labs public research discussion card (P24) proposing an assumption-kill experiment to test whether Exendin-4 retains neuroprotective or cognitive phenotype (≥50% of the Exendin-4 without-GLP1R-abolish arm) under conditions where GLP1R-class attribution is fully abolished via exendin-9-39 antagonism or Glp1r genetic loss-of-function. The document is a pre-registered hypothesis/assay proposal at TRL 1–2, with no experimental data yet generated (execution_status=NOT_RUN). Existing literature (During, Perry, McClean, Serre, Jia/Gong, Zhang, Basalay) provides prior art that leans against a residual phenotype, and the matched residual H2H result is explicitly UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Document Overview and Claim
content_blocks.content: Mol Labs public report (P24) framing Exendin-4 neuroprotection/cognition as potentially exceeding GLP1R-class attribution. The core claim: on a matched rodent cognition/neuroprotection panel (During/Perry/McClean-class) ± Exendin-4 ± GLP1R antagonist (exendin-9-39) or Glp1r genetic LOF titrated to abolish GLP1R-class neuroprotection/cognition attribution, residual Exendin-4 neuroprotective/cognitive phenotype remains ≥50% of the Exendin-4 without-GLP1R-abolish arm. This is labeled an 'assumption-kill / glp1r-insufficiency' experiment. Execution status: NOT_RUN. The result is explicitly UNKNOWN — no experimental data have been generated.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch and Scientific Rationale
content_blocks.content: The rationale draws on four key literature anchors: (1) During (PMID 12925848): Glp1r LOF causes learning deficit and enhanced kainate neuronal injury; agonist benefit is through GLP-1R — argues necessity AGAINST residual. (2) Perry (PMID 12183643): Exendin-4 excitotoxic neuroprotection phenotype established, but no residual-under-abolish arm. (3) McClean (PMID 21525299): liraglutide AD cognition phenotype — class phenotype, not Ex4 residual under abolish. (4) Serre (PMID 9794451): Exendin-(9-39) is a murine GLP-1R inverse agonist — tool prior, not CNS residual H2H. Three promoted (out-of-public-prior-art) references lean AGAINST residual: Jia/Gong (PMID 26546042) — exenatide MCAO neuroprotection completely blocked by exendin(9-39); Zhang (PMID 37595875) — Exendin-4 CA1 excitation completely blocked by exendin(9-39); Basalay (PMID 31721014) — semaglutide neuroprotection abolished by exendin(9-39).

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay Design
content_blocks.content: Proposed experimental design: matched rodent cognition/neuroprotection panel (During/Perry/McClean-class) with four arms: (1) vehicle, (2) Exendin-4 alone, (3) GLP1R antagonist (exendin-9-39) or Glp1r genetic LOF alone, (4) Exendin-4 + GLP1R antagonist/LOF. Block must be titrated to abolish GLP1R-class neuroprotection/cognition attribution before scoring residual. Preferred sequence: cell/slice/block-QC with exendin-9-39 or Glp1r ablation first, then in vivo panel (in vivo remains primary kill path). Readout: neuroprotective or cognitive endpoint. Threshold: residual Exendin-4 phenotype ≥50% of Exendin-4 without-GLP1R-abolish arm. α/N pre-specified. Kill cost tier: 1. Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: glp1r-insufficiency. Vault hold: no.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria and Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content: Refute if: on the pre-registered matched panel, residual Exendin-4 neuroprotective/cognitive phenotype is <50% of the Exendin-4 without-GLP1R-abolish arm, after ruling out abolish-fail, Exendin-4-alone-null, underpowered strata, or assay-mismatch artifacts. Key limitations: (1) Do not treat P1–P23 as proving P24; (2) Do not collapse to skip-list compounds (BPC-157/FBXO22, LKKTETQ, MOTS-c, SS-31, ARA290, Semax/TrkB, Selank/GABA, Dihexa/c-Met, oxytocin/OXTR); (3) Do not misread Glp1r gene-transfer rescue as Exendin-4 residual under GLP1R abolish; (4) Do not invent residual when UNKNOWN; (5) Do not treat necessity as residual-positive; (6) NOT FOXO4×LOF (SERIES_FROZEN); (7) Reviews ≠ experimental anchors; (8) No dosing specified.

content_blocks.title: Series Distinctness and Skip-List
content_blocks.content: P24 is explicitly distinct from: P15 (BPC residual-FBXO22), P16 (LKKTETQ-Cc), P17 (MOTS-c/folate), P18 (SS-31/ROS-scavenger), P19 (ARA290/IRR), P20 (Semax/TrkB; Exendin-4≠Semax; GLP1R≠TrkB), P21 (Selank/GABA; Exendin-4≠Selank; GLP1R≠GABA), P22 (Dihexa/c-Met; Exendin-4≠Dihexa; GLP1R≠c-Met), P23 (oxytocin/OXTR; Exendin-4≠oxytocin; GLP1R≠OXTR). orthosteric_drift=false. NOT FOXO4×LOF. Soft-complete empty ≠ novelty / ≠ failure.

content_blocks.title: Execution and IP Status
content_blocks.content: Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Kill cost tier: 1 (cheap IP). Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: glp1r-insufficiency. Vault hold: no. Status label: NEGATIVE. Polarity: negative. Risk class: research-discussion. Dual-publish status: PENDING.

key_findings: Execution status is NOT_RUN — no experimental data have been generated for P24; the matched residual H2H result is explicitly UNKNOWN.

The core hypothesis (P24) asks whether Exendin-4 retains ≥50% neuroprotective/cognitive phenotype under GLP1R-abolish conditions (exendin-9-39 or Glp1r LOF) compared to Exendin-4 without-GLP1R-abolish arm on the same panel.

All existing literature leans AGAINST residual: During (PMID 12925848) shows Glp1r necessity for learning/neuroprotection; Jia/Gong (PMID 26546042) shows exenatide MCAO neuroprotection completely blocked by exendin(9-39); Zhang (PMID 37595875) shows Exendin-4 CA1 excitation completely blocked by exendin(9-39); Basalay (PMID 31721014) shows semaglutide neuroprotection abolished by exendin(9-39).
Perry (PMID 12183643) establishes Exendin-4 excitotoxic neuroprotection phenotype in cultured rat hippocampal neurons and in vivo, but lacks an Ex9-39/Glp1r-/- residual arm.

McClean (PMID 21525299) establishes liraglutide AD cognition phenotype in APP/PS1 mice (object recognition, water maze, synapse loss, plaque pathology), but liraglutide ≠ Exendin-4 and no residual-under-abolish arm exists.
Serre (PMID 9794451) validates Exendin-(9-39) as a murine GLP-1R inverse agonist tool (lowers basal cAMP, impairs GSIS in βTC-Tet), but this is a pancreatic/metabolic context, not CNS residual H2H.

Proposed assay: cell/slice/block-QC with exendin-9-39 or Glp1r ablation preferred before new animal During/Perry/McClean-class cognition/neuroprotection panels; in vivo panel remains primary kill path.
Refutation threshold: residual Exendin-4 phenotype <50% of Exendin-4 without-GLP1R-abolish arm (after ruling out abolish-fail, Ex4-alone-null, underpowered, or assay-mismatch artifacts).
Kill cost tier: 1; estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; IP class: glp1r-insufficiency; vault hold: no.
Status label: NEGATIVE; polarity: negative — the prior art weight leans against the residual hypothesis.
